events.title: Another ransomware case in the sector
events.body: Another comparable business has been extorted. Most of these cases began with a managed service provider's privileged access. The tradecraft is consistent and unremarkable, which is what makes it effective.

variants.title: Ransomware again in the sector
variants.body: Another business like ours has been encrypted and extorted. The way in was a supplier's remote access, as it has been in most of these.

variants.title: A peer's warehouses are down
variants.body: A comparable logistics business has had its warehouse systems encrypted. Their managed service provider's administrator accounts were the way in. They expect to be down for weeks.

variants.title: The same technique, another victim
variants.body: The ransomware reports from the sector have stopped being surprising: in through supplier access, across on privileged accounts, backups first, then encryption. Another business has been through it.

events.title: Credential campaign against sector portals
events.body: Criminals are trying stolen passwords against partner login pages across the sector, a few at a time so they stay under the lockout limits. Volumes are high, and they are patient.

variants.title: The password campaign is still running
variants.body: The campaign trying stolen passwords against the sector's partner portals has not stopped. It has slowed, spread across more addresses, and become harder to see.

variants.title: Partner portals: the attempts continue
variants.body: Intelligence partners report another wave of password attempts against partner and supplier portals in the sector. Low and slow, under the lockout limits, from addresses that change by the hour.

variants.title: Stolen passwords, patiently tried
variants.body: The credential campaign against sector portals has moved on to newer password lists. Anyone who reuses a password from a breached website is being tried, a login at a time.

events.title: Working exploit published for the checkout framework
events.body: Proof-of-concept code was published overnight for the framework version running our checkout service. It is reliable and it is already being used opportunistically.

events.title: Briefing: patient collection against data platforms
events.body: A government briefing describes an actor collecting behavioural and commercial data sets from analytics providers over periods of a year or more. Detection in the reported cases came from partners, not from the victims.

events.title: Anomalous vendor access, three nights running
events.body: Vendor remote access sessions at 03:40 on three consecutive nights, outside Corvus's contracted hours. Analyst confidence is low; the account behaviour is not conclusively abnormal. Raising it because the pattern is consistent.

events.title: Targeted phishing against finance
events.body: Finance staff received a convincing invoice lure this morning. At least one person entered credentials before it was reported. The account has been reset.

variants.title: The invoice lures are back
variants.body: The invoice lures are back, better written this time, and aimed at accounts payable. Somebody entered their password before the report came in. The account is reset and the session ended.

variants.title: Phishing against the finance team
variants.body: A supplier-payment lure reached the finance team this morning, sent from a lookalike of a real supplier's domain. Somebody gave up their credentials; we reset the account within the hour.

variants.title: Credentials entered on a fake login page
variants.body: A convincing payment-approval email sent finance staff to a fake sign-in page. At least one person used it before we saw the pattern. The account is reset and the page reported for takedown.

events.title: Engineers targeted with package lures
events.body: Three engineers received messages referencing an internal repository and a package update. The lure is well researched: it names a real project and a real colleague.

events.title: Sustained scanning of the partner portal
events.body: Automated scanning against the partner portal is running continuously from a rotating set of addresses. Nothing has succeeded. Yet.

variants.title: The portal is being scanned again
variants.body: Scanning against the partner portal has picked up again, from a fresh set of addresses. It is working over the sign-in and password reset pages. Nothing has got through.

variants.title: Background noise on the partner portal
variants.body: Automated probes against the partner portal carry on around the clock. Most of it is the internet's background noise; some of it is looking specifically for the software we run.

variants.title: Someone is mapping the partner portal
variants.body: The scanning against the partner portal has become more methodical: fewer addresses, slower, working through the pages in order. Still nothing has succeeded. It is the pattern we would expect before somebody tries properly.

events.title: High-severity alerts turn out to be benign
events.body: A cluster of high-severity alerts from the corporate network overnight came from an internal system misconfigured into looking like an attack. Several analyst hours, and nothing wrong.

variants.title: The print server again
variants.body: Last night's high-severity alerts were the misconfigured print server scanning the network again. Benign. Nobody has fixed it because it is nobody's job, and the analysts are starting to skim anything from that part of the network.

variants.title: False alarm, overnight
variants.body: The overnight alerts on the corporate network were benign: a misconfigured internal system that looks, to our tooling, exactly like an intruder mapping the network. We confirmed it the slow way, which is the only way we have.

variants.title: Benign, after a long night
variants.body: Critical alerts overnight, traced by morning to the same misconfigured print server. The analysts would like it fixed. They know that on the night it is not the printer, they will be tempted to assume it is.

events.title: Escalation quality review
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: Of 340 escalations last quarter, 318 were false positives. The team has started closing them without reading properly. That is a control failure, and it is ours rather than the provider's.

events.title: Nexora credentials found in a breach dump
events.body: Corporate email addresses with passwords have turned up in a credential dump from an unrelated breach. Some of them match accounts that are still active here.

variants.title: More Nexora credentials for sale
variants.body: A new credential dump on a criminal marketplace includes Nexora email addresses with passwords. Some of them are old. Some of them still match live accounts.

variants.title: Staff passwords in somebody else's breach
variants.body: Staff who used their work email to sign up to an unrelated website have had their passwords published in that site's breach. Where they reused the password here, it is now public.

variants.title: Credentials in circulation
variants.body: Another list of Nexora addresses and passwords is circulating. Where multi-factor authentication is enforced this is an inconvenience; where it is not, it is an open door.

events.title: A supplier in the sector has been compromised
events.body: A managed service provider serving several businesses in this sector has disclosed a compromise. Corvus is not named. Corvus uses the same remote access product.

events.title: Threat hunt found nothing
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: The hunt came back clean. That is genuinely good news, with the caveat that we hunted where we have telemetry, which is not everywhere.

events.title: The activity has stopped
events.body: The pattern we were tracking has stopped. Either the activity moved on, or it moved somewhere we cannot see.

events.title: Warehouse systems named in a vendor advisory
events.body: The vendor of the Meridian warehouse platform has issued an advisory for a remotely exploitable flaw. There is no patch for the version we run, and there will not be one.

events.title: An access pattern that does not fit a role
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: An analyst in the commercial team has been querying the data lake at volumes well beyond their role. It is most likely enthusiasm rather than malice, but somebody has to ask.

events.title: A detection worked
events.body: A privileged session from an unusual source was flagged and challenged within eleven minutes. The account belonged to a contractor whose engagement had ended. Nothing further happened.

events.title: We would not have seen it
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: We replayed a public incident against our own telemetry. On our current coverage we would have detected step four of five, about nine days in.

events.title: A peer paid
events.body: One of the extorted businesses in the sector paid, and it has become public. The commentary is unkind. The board will have read it.

events.title: Something is probing the test environment
events.body: An exposed service in the non-production tenancy is being probed persistently. It is only a test environment, which is the reason nobody has looked at what it can reach.

events.title: Advisory: build pipelines as an attack route
events.body: A national advisory describes actors using continuous delivery pipelines to deploy their own access into production. The technique relies on standing credentials in the pipeline.
